key_insight: In quantitative finance—not materials discovery—a bounded LLM research loop prioritizes rejecting false discoveries over maximizing backtest performance.
engineering_relevance: The architecture illustrates how trusted evaluation code, restricted proposals and auditable records can constrain AI-driven experimental search.
method: Limit model proposals to declarative JSON over a fixed vocabulary; trusted code runs evaluations.
Separate immutable data into discovery, validation and a one-use final holdout.
Require multiple acceptance gates, reject duplicates and log proposals, refusals, crashes and results in a hash-chained ledger.
evidence_signal: Across roughly two dozen finance campaigns, two results survived pre-registered bars, while one candidate with discovery and validation Sharpe ratios near 3 dropped to 0.26 on holdout.
watch_item: Passing historical gates does not establish future profitability; market drift remains a concern.
paper_title: Hard to Fool: A Bounded LLM Research Loop for Quantitative Finance, and What Two Dozen Campaigns Found
